item.title: Takaichi Defends Absence From G7 Online Call After Criticism
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi defended her absence from a Group of Seven online meeting, responding over social media to some critics who questioned why she didn’t attend despite her apparently free schedule.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: Quebec Separatists Win Power in New Challenge for Canada’s Carney
item.description: Voters in Quebec elected a separatist political party for the first time in more than a decade, setting the stage for more strained relations with Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government and an eventual referendum on the province’s independence from Canada.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion

item.title: Trump Eases Limits on Dyed Diesel in Bid to Cut Fuel Costs
item.description: President Donald Trump on Monday signed an executive order to ease restrictions on the use of a tax-exempt variety of diesel, his latest bid to pare costs for the fuel ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Josh Wingrove

item.title: Bond Selloff to Pressure Australia’s Budget, Chalmers Says
item.description: Higher global bond yields will put pressure on the Australian budget as the widespread selloff pushes debt refinancing costs higher, Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers warned on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger and Matthew Burgess

item.title: US Moves Bombers From UK Airbase as Threats Linger
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Mark Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, says the Senate Intelligence Committee was not briefed about US bombers leaving a UK base and says lawmakers are not receiving regular updates on the conflict with Iran. Heather Conley, senior fellow at AEI, a senior advisor at Evenflow Macro LLC and a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, says conflicting explanations from the administration over the movement of US bombers from the UK's Fairford airbase raise questions about the military's ability to protect its assets. Patrick McHenry, Former House Financial Services Chair and Speaker Pro Tempore, says Republicans are playing defense in the 2026 midterms as campaign money moves toward races the party considers more urgent to protect. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Vows to Pay for Ads Praising Him With Personal, PAC Funds
item.description: President Donald Trump pledged to pay for video ads with his personal funds — and money from his super political action committee — following ethical concerns about the messages that are running at taxpayer expense.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Josh Wingrove

item.title: McHenry Says Debt Fight Could Hit Treasuries Harder
item.description: Patrick McHenry, Former House Financial Services Chair, says Republicans are playing defense in the 2026 midterms as campaign money moves toward races the party considers more urgent to protect. McHenry says Republicans should address the debt ceiling while they control Congress and the White House, warning Democrats could use it as leverage next year and that another standoff could cause greater Treasury-market turmoil than the 2023 fight. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Conley: Refined Fuels Remain The Energy Problem
item.description: Heather Conley, senior fellow at AEI, a senior advisor at Evenflow Macro LLC and a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, says conflicting explanations from the administration over the movement of US bombers from the UK's Fairford airbase raise questions about the military's ability to protect its assets. Conley says improved crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz do not solve the energy problem because supplies of refined products remain constrained. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Warner Says Senate Not Briefed On B-1 Bomber Move
item.description: Sen. Mark Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, says the Senate Intelligence Committee was not briefed about US bombers leaving a UK base and says lawmakers are not receiving regular updates on the conflict with Iran. Sen. Warner says the move could give Iran a propaganda win by allowing it to claim it drove the US away from an allied airbase and warns Iran could continue to extract a toll on oil, diesel, aluminum and fertilizer. Sen. Warner also says AI needs mandatory safety testing while the US continues to compete with China. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: S&P Edges Towards Record (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
US stocks extended gains on Monday as investors weighed resilient earnings expectations against mounting bond-market and political worries. The S&P 500 inched closer to a record high despite the benchmark Treasury yield spiking to the highest in more than two decades. The stock gauge has gained roughly 14% since the beginning of the year.
On today's episode:
Ed Harrison, Bloomberg News Senior Strategist Laura Nahmias, Bloomberg News Senior Reporter & Seth Fiegerman, Bloomberg News AI Editor Sumit Roy, Realty Income CEO Dylan Sloan, Bloomberg News Wealth Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Treasury Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Kestra Investment Management Chief Investment Officer Kara Murphy, Vanguard Senior Fixed Income Client Portfolio Manager Joyce Huang, BofA Securities Senior Equity Research Analyst Wamsi Mohan, CH Robinson President & CEO Dave Bozeman, Former Boston Fed President Eric Rosengren, Pivotal Advisors CEO & CIO Tiffany McGhee, UBS Chief Investment Office Fixed Income Strategy Head Leslie Falconio, CHANGE Global Founder & Managing Director Thea Jamison, Coresight Research Founder & CEO Deborah Weinswig, & Babylist CEO Jennifer Hyman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Pays $950 Million to Buy California ICE Jails From Geo Group
item.description: The Trump administration agreed to pay $950 million to buy three California immigration detention facilities from GEO Group Inc., part of a broader push to give the federal government more direct control over the infrastructure behind its mass deportation campaign.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Fmr. Boston Fed Pres: Waiting To Raise Rates Seems Right
item.description: Former Boston Fed President Eric Rosengren described the U.S. economy as middling: inflation has eased more than policymakers expected at their September meeting, while the latest jobs report was somewhat weak. He said the Fed is likely to wait until its final meeting of the year before deciding whether another 25-basis-point hike is needed, rather than act just before the midterm elections. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Elecciones Brasil: Lula replantea su campaña ante Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Read the story in English
item.dc:creator: Simone Iglesias, Martha Beck and Andrew Rosati

item.title: Brazil’s Right-Wing Shift Highlights a Bigger Trend
item.description: Brazil’s turn to the right matches the ideological switch across Latin America, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Juan Pablo Spinetto says. A Bolsonaro triumph in the runoff would mark the seventh consecutive win by a right-wing presidential candidate in the region in the past year, proof that beyond the problems facing incumbents, a deeper philosophical shift is afoot. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Yemen Forces Recapture Mocha From Houthis, Eye Bab el-Mandeb Control
item.description: Yemen’s armed forces wrested control of the Red Sea city of Mocha on Monday after battles with the Iran-backed Houthis, according to state-run Saba, which puts the internationally recognized government closer to taking over the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: White House Blocks Politico From Air Force One Trip
item.description: The White House is refusing to allow Politico to travel Monday on Air Force One with President Donald Trump, the latest salvo in a fight that has seen officials restrict access to certain media outlets.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Hannah Miller

item.title: Trump Says Terror Threats Forced B-1 Bombers Out of UK Base
item.description: President Donald Trump said fresh threats of terror attacks prompted the US to move its B-1 bombers from their base in the UK, contradicting his top diplomat who had earlier described the move as part of a regular rotation.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Ellen Milligan

item.title: Obama Plans Detroit Rally With El-Sayed in Tight Senate Race
item.description: Former President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump both plan to campaign in Michigan during the coming weeks in a showdown to bolster their candidates, especially in the key Senate race between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and opponent Mike Rogers, just ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
item.dc:creator: David Welch

item.title: Germany, France Push New Trade Weapon Before EU-China Talks
item.description: Germany and France are urging the European Union to adopt new powers that could cut China or other countries off from the bloc’s single market, risking a response from Beijing days before key talks on trade imbalances and other disputes.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs and Jorge Valero
